David Jolly

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Florida · Open seat

Attorney; former U.S. Representative

David Jolly is a former Republican congressman who represented Florida's 13th District from 2014 to 2017. He later spent about six years as an independent before registering as a Democrat. He is the Democratic nominee for Florida governor in the open-seat race on November 3, 2026, with former U.S. Rep. Gwen Graham as his running mate for lieutenant governor.

Where Jolly stands

Property insurance
Proposes a state-backed catastrophic or disaster fund to lower homeowners' insurance costs. His campaign says the plan would cut premiums by 60 to 70 percent.
Property taxes
Opposes Amendment 3, the property tax ballot measure. Says he understands that 'people are begging for property tax relief.'
Campaign priorities
Names housing, health care, education and opposition to data centers as his top campaign priorities.
Housing
Proposes investing in workforce and affordable housing.
Education / school choice
Supports keeping school choice under new rules. Says voucher schools should have to teach reading and offer college-prep, trades or arts classes, and should meet the same standards as public schools.
Education / teacher pay
Supports raising teacher pay. Proposes a nonpartisan task force to write a 10-year plan for public education.
Health care
Supports expanding Medicaid. Also supports expanding access to primary care through community health clinics, nonprofits and federally qualified health centers.
Abortion
Says Florida's abortion restrictions are too strict, and says he will respect the will of the voters.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Florida's 13th Congressional District (R), 2014–2017
  • Left the Republican Party and was an independent for about six years; later registered as a Democrat
  • Occupation: attorney
  • Education: B.A. in History, Emory University (1994); J.D. cum laude, George Mason University (2001)
  • Residence: Indian Rocks Beach
